jobs.verdict: reads as the edge if you know what to look for
jobs.edge_reads_as: A (formal impossibility) with strong K (inaccessible state) overlap
jobs.paragraph: The plate establishes a clear bounded formal system (wireframe walls) containing provable truths (walkable floor) and unreachable truths (elevated islands across void gaps). The spatial grammar is sound: the void is structural, not bridgeable. However, the teaching moment is dilu
hints: Move godel_statement_plaque onto one of the unreachable islands—the self-referential statement should physically occupy the unprovable space
Rotate spawn to face directly toward islands so player immediately confronts unreachable truth
Replace full wireframe with solid walls and wireframe only on islands to make them visually pop
Add a broken bridge or ladder stopping mid-void—showing attempted connection structurally fails
Echo plaque text across the void: statement visible on main floor, truth on unreachable island—spatial encoding of 'expressible but unprovable'
Make teleporter appear only after player reads plaque and confronts the gap—exit becomes acknowledgment of incompleteness

jobs.edge_reads_as: A or D—search algorithms in general, not tractability limits
jobs.paragraph: This plate reads as an introduction to search algorithms—BFS, DFS, Dijkstra—not as a demonstration of tractability collapse. All three artifacts appear at similar, comfortable scales (a small grid, a simple maze, a ~15-node graph), with no visual progression from 'solvable' to 'i
hints: Replace three distinct algorithms with one problem (e.g., traveling salesperson) at three scales: N=5, N=8, N=12
Use vertical stacking or spatial volume to encode search tree growth—N=12 should be visibly denser or taller than N=5
Make the largest instance overflow its grid bounds or spawn geometry that reaches toward the ceiling
Position the player path to walk past N=5 (instant solution), N=8 (slower), N=12 (visibly struggling or incomplete)
Consider a bespoke 'search tree visualizer' artifact that grows branches in real-time—player watches N=5 finish, then N=12 fills the room before timing out
Use artifact density as the teaching variable: same footprint, exponentially more geometry per step in N

jobs.edge_reads_as: unclear — reads as 'optimization landscape in general' rather than specifically Edge C's local-versus-global trap; could also read as Edge E (dimensionality reduction) due to the 3D projection
jobs.paragraph: The map establishes the loss landscape as physical terrain — the fundamental metaphor is present and walkable. The purple gradient surface with wireframe mesh reads clearly as a mathematical function made spatial. However, the plate fails to make the trap visceral: multiple minim
hints: Make 3-4 distinct valleys visible from spawn, each a different depth and with distinct color-coding (e.g., green for shallow local minima, deep blue for the global minimum)
Place the teleporter visibly in a valley separated from spawn by a ridge — the 'you can see it but can't walk there' moment must be unmistakable
Remove or drastically reduce the particle clouds — they obscure the surface and read as noise rather than structure
Add a visible descent trail or animated walker showing a path that converges into a local minimum while the teleporter glows in a different valley
Simplify or remove the perimeter terraced structures — they compete for attention without teaching the edge
Consider height-coding the valleys with labels or floating markers: 'local minimum' vs. 'global minimum' to make the hierarchy explicit without text-on-walls

jobs.paragraph: The map reads as a sparse exhibition floor rather than a teaching plate. Edge D requires visible sorting, categorization, and exclusion—a Vesalius-cousin diagram where the unlabeled region becomes the argument. This space has the grid infrastructure (pink lines suggesting measure
hints: Add central sorting artifact: a classifier with labeled bins where the player category is conspicuously absent
Use Vesalius pattern: place a detailed anatomical/typological diagram with one region deliberately unlabeled or greyed out
Show feature extraction visually: pedestals measuring height, color, shape—with visible gaps in what's measured
Position unlabeled silhouette or data point at path center, surrounded by fully-labeled examples
Consider boolean-cut vocabulary: show the positive space of categories, make the excluded region a literal void
Add weight: the plate should be dense enough to read as diagram, not empty stage

jobs.paragraph: The map's spatial grammar—discrete purple wireframe grid suspended in black void—sets up the continuous-discrete tension, but the plate fails because its teaching artifacts are missing or non-functional. The blurb promises floating hands in a mirror with nail customization, yet t
hints: Fix color_picker artifact reference—ensure it spawns and is reachable from spawn point
Add VR hand models at spawn or as ghost poses frozen in mid-gesture—make the 'fragments in void' literal
Position mirror at eye level, 2-3 cells from spawn, facing player—reflection should be unavoidable first sight
Mirror surface should show hands clearly, possibly with grid overlay or wireframe skin to emphasize quantization
Replace placeholder cubes with the actual teaching artifacts or remove them entirely
Consider dual mirrors: one showing continuous hand tracking, one showing grid-snapped positions—the mismatch IS the plate

jobs.edge_reads_as: G (parameter space as landscape) or E (emergence at threshold)
jobs.paragraph: This map teaches parameter-space-as-landscape (Edge G) or emergence-at-threshold (Edge E), not apparatus-as-phenomenon (Edge H). The λ gradient is visually clear—order to edge to chaos—and the corridor makes it walkable, but the phenomenon appears pre-existing rather than enacted
hints: Add a central phenomenon that reads as 'ordered crystal' when approached from the λ=0 end, 'chaotic particle cloud' when approached from the λ=1 end—same object, different apparatus-cuts
Split the corridor into two parallel paths (one ordered-frame, one chaotic-frame) that yield contradictory measurements of the same centerline phenomenon
Make the gradient visibly responsive to player attention: the phenomenon at position X changes when you look at it vs when you turn away
Place measurement apparatus artifacts (frames, lenses, grids) along the path that are visibly part of what they're measuring—the frame and the framed as one system
Show the 'cut' that produces observer and observed: a bifurcation point where the path's choice determines which phenomenon appears ahead

jobs.paragraph: The plate teaches synthesis and convergence across multiple optimization regimes, which is the antithesis of Edge L. Where L demands visible refusal to converge, this map shows three parallel islands each running optimization pipelines (RL walker, generative model, classifier) wi
hints: Replace the central optimization tracker with a hill that agents visibly ignore or walk away from
Place 'failed' artifacts (Twombly scribbles, non-converging patterns, Darger cosmologies) on lower terraces with richer visual detail than anything at the peak
Show one agent thrashing indefinitely while beautiful complexity accrues in its wake — make the thrashing itself the artifact
Add a teleporter that unlocks only when player stops trying to reach the summit
Include a gradient descent path that deliberately leads to a 'worse' loss value where something unexpected blooms
Replace loss-tracking graphs with Hokusai manga pages — studies that never arrive at final form
Stage a Q-learning table that refuses to converge, with the non-convergence generating a fractal pattern
